subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: Which princely state was the first part of India to hold an election based on universal adult franchise in June 1948 under Maharaja Bodhachandra Singh?
questions.explanation: Manipur held legislative assembly elections based on universal adult franchise in June 1948, becoming the first region in India to do so.

questions.question: The Swatantra Party, which advocated free market enterprise and minimal government control over the economy, was founded in August 1959 by:
questions.explanation: C. Rajagopalachari founded the Swatantra Party in August 1959 to champion individual freedom, free enterprise, and private property rights.

questions.question: In which month and year was the National Development Council (NDC) set up to approve Five Year Plans and foster cooperative federalism?
questions.explanation: The National Development Council (NDC) was established by an executive resolution on 6 August 1952, comprising the Prime Minister, Union Cabinet Ministers, and Chief Ministers of all states.

questions.question: In which year did the Tibetan spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, cross over the border and seek political asylum in India along with thousands of followers?
questions.explanation: The 14th Dalai Lama fled Tibet and sought political asylum in India in March 1959 following the suppression of the Tibetan uprising by Chinese troops.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Following the 1969 split in the Indian National Congress, the faction led by Indira Gandhi came to be known as:
questions.explanation: The Congress split into Congress (Organisation) led by the Syndicate and Congress (Requisitionists) led by Indira Gandhi in November 1969.

questions.question: At which historic public venue in Patna did Jayaprakash Narayan give the call for 'Sampoorna Kranti' (Total Revolution) in June 1974?
questions.explanation: On 5 June 1974, Jayaprakash Narayan addressed a mammoth rally of students and citizens at Gandhi Maidan in Patna, proclaiming the call for Total Revolution.

questions.question: The Punjab Accord signed in July 1985 to restore peace in Punjab is officially known as the:
questions.explanation: The Punjab Accord was signed on 24 July 1985 between Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and Akali Dal President Sant Harchand Singh Longowal.

questions.question: The Anti-Arrack Movement, a spontaneous grassroots campaign against the sale of country liquor, was spearheaded by rural women in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The Anti-Arrack movement began in village Dubagunta in Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh in 1992 during an adult literacy programme.

questions.question: In August 1990, which Indian Prime Minister announced the Union Government's decision to implement the Mandal Commission recommendation of 27% reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs)?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Vishwanath Pratap Singh announced the implementation of 27% job reservations for OBCs in the Lok Sabha on 7 August 1990.

questions.question: Which constitutional amendment act granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions (rural local governments) in India in 1992?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 inserted Part IX into the Constitution, giving constitutional recognition to the three-tier Panchayati Raj system.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: The Southeast Asia Treaty Organization (SEATO), established in 1954 under US leadership, was formally created through a treaty signed in which capital city?
questions.explanation: The Manila Pact (Southeast Asia Collective Defense Treaty) was signed in Manila on 8 September 1954, establishing SEATO.

questions.question: Which regional organization was formed in December 1991 by the leaders of Russia, Belarus, and Ukraine following the dissolution of the Soviet Union?
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) was founded in December 1991 under the Belavezha Accords and expanded through the Alma-Ata Protocol.

questions.question: Which US military operation involved missile strikes against terrorist targets in Sudan and Afghanistan in 1998 under President Bill Clinton?
questions.explanation: Operation Infinite Reach was launched by the US military in August 1998, firing cruise missiles at Al-Qaeda targets in Sudan and Afghanistan in retaliation for embassy bombings in Kenya and Tanzania.

questions.question: In which year was the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) established to coordinate security and foreign policy dialogue across the Asia-Pacific region?
questions.explanation: The ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) was launched in 1994 to facilitate regional security consultations among ASEAN member states and dialogue partners.

questions.question: The Bangladesh Liberation War of December 1971 resulted in the formal surrender of Pakistani armed forces in Dhaka under Lieutenant General:
questions.explanation: Lieutenant General A.A.K. Niazi signed the Instrument of Surrender on 16 December 1971 in Dhaka before Lieutenant General Jagjit Singh Aurora of the joint Indian and Bangladesh forces.

questions.question: The veteran Gandhian leader whose 58-day hunger strike resulted in his martyrdom and forced the creation of the linguistic state of Andhra in 1953 was:
questions.explanation: Potti Sreeramulu began an indefinite hunger strike demanding a separate Andhra state for Telugu-speaking people, dying on 15 December 1952 after 58 days of fasting.

questions.question: In 1964, the Communist Party of India (CPI) underwent a major split, giving birth to the Communist Party of India (Marxist) primarily due to ideological differences concerning:
options: A) The Sino-Soviet ideological dispute and relations with the Congress government
B) Disagreements over the adoption of the Constitution of India
C) Disputes over whether to participate in parliamentary elections
D) Differences over supporting the linguistic reorganisation of states
questions.explanation: The 1964 split in the CPI was precipitated by ideological polarities between the pro-Moscow faction (CPI) and the pro-Beijing/more radical anti-Congress faction (CPI-M).

questions.question: Under whose leadership was the rural dairy cooperative model of Anand (Amul) developed, giving rise to the nationwide 'Operation Flood' in 1970?
questions.explanation: Dr. Verghese Kurien, known as the 'Milkman of India', headed the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) and spearheaded Operation Flood to make India the world's largest milk producer.

questions.question: In August 1971, facing the looming Bangladesh crisis and the US-China-Pakistan diplomatic axis, India signed a 20-year Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation with:
questions.explanation: India and the USSR signed the landmark 20-year Indo-Soviet Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation on 9 August 1971, providing India diplomatic and strategic deterrence against third-party intervention.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: The famous political expression 'Aaya Ram, Gaya Ram' became part of Indian political lexicon following the repeated floor-crossing by Gaya Lal, an MLA from which state in 1967?
questions.explanation: Gaya Lal, an independent MLA in Haryana, switched parties thrice within a fortnight in 1967, prompting Congress leader Rao Birender Singh to announce: 'Gaya Ram is now Aaya Ram'.

questions.question: The Navnirman Movement in Gujarat, which broke out in January 1974 leading to the resignation of Chief Minister Chimanbhai Patel, was originally initiated by:
options: A) University and engineering students protesting against foodgrain price hikes and hostel charges
B) Industrial trade unions demanding higher minimum wages
C) Farmers protesting land ceiling legislation
D) Government servants demanding Dearness Allowance increments
questions.explanation: The Navnirman Movement in Gujarat began in January 1974 when students at the L.D. College of Engineering in Ahmedabad protested a 20% hike in hostel food charges, expanding into a state-wide agitation.

questions.question: Which special provision of the Constitution of India historically conferred temporary autonomous status upon the State of Jammu and Kashmir until its abrogation in August 2019?
questions.explanation: Article 370 of the Indian Constitution granted special autonomous status to Jammu and Kashmir, restricting Parliament's legislative powers over the state to defense, foreign affairs, finance, and communications.

questions.question: The Narmada Bachao Andolan (NBA), spearheaded by Medha Patkar, focused primarily on demanding rehabilitation and environmental justice concerning the construction of:
questions.explanation: The Narmada Bachao Andolan protested against the Sardar Sarovar Dam on the Narmada River in Gujarat, highlighting the displacement of indigenous populations and ecological submergence.

questions.question: Following the 1996 general elections, the United Front formed a coalition government with outside support from the Congress, headed by Prime Minister:
questions.explanation: Haradanahalli Doddegowda Deve Gowda (H.D. Deve Gowda) became Prime Minister of the 13-party United Front coalition in June 1996, supported from outside by the Congress party.

questions.question: Who served as the very first Secretary-General of the United Nations from 1946 to 1952?
questions.explanation: Trygve Lie, a Norwegian diplomat and politician, was chosen as the first UN Secretary-General in February 1946 and served until his resignation in November 1952.

questions.question: Which international non-governmental organization was founded in London in 1961 by lawyer Peter Benenson to campaign for the defense of prisoners of conscience worldwide?
questions.explanation: Amnesty International was established in 1961 by Peter Benenson following the publication of his article 'The Forgotten Prisoners', campaigning for the release of prisoners of conscience.

questions.question: The Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC), which bans the development, production, stockpiling, and use of chemical weapons, was opened for signature in Paris in:
questions.explanation: The Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC) was signed in Paris in January 1993 and entered into force in April 1997, overseen by the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW).

questions.question: Under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) of 1968, a 'Nuclear Weapon State' is defined as any state that manufactured and exploded a nuclear weapon prior to:
questions.explanation: Article IX of the NPT restricts the definition of a Nuclear Weapon State to those nations that tested a nuclear device prior to 1 January 1967 (US, USSR, UK, France, and China).

questions.question: Which landmark international environmental agreement, signed in 1987, mandated the phase-out of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and other ozone-depleting substances?
questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer was agreed upon on 16 September 1987 to protect the stratospheric ozone layer.

questions.question: The Antarctic Treaty signed in Washington in December 1959 explicitly mandates that Antarctica shall be used exclusively for:
options: A) Commercial mining exploration and oil extraction by signatory nations
B) Peaceful scientific investigations, prohibiting military measures and nuclear explosions
C) Permanent sovereign territorial claims by adjacent Southern Hemisphere states
D) Exclusive military surveillance bases and defense testing
questions.explanation: The Antarctic Treaty of 1959 demilitarized the Antarctic continent, banned nuclear testing and radioactive waste disposal, and preserved it for peaceful scientific cooperation.

questions.question: Globalisation is fundamentally defined as a multidimensional phenomenon characterized by the intensification of worldwide flows of:
options: A) Military armaments and nuclear warheads exclusively
B) Unrestricted physical border demolitions under a single world government
C) Ideas, capital, commodities, and people across national borders
D) Nationalized state industries replacing private corporate enterprises
questions.explanation: NCERT defines globalisation as a multi-dimensional concept involving interconnected flows of ideas, capital, commodities, and people across borders, impacting political, economic, and cultural spheres.

questions.question: The Master of Business Administration (MBA) degree, an emblem of US structural hegemony in world education, originated at which business school established in 1881?
options: B) Stanford Graduate School of Business
D) Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania
questions.explanation: The Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania was founded in 1881 as the first collegiate business school in the world, pioneering formal management degrees.

questions.question: In 1980, the Chinese government established four Special Economic Zones (SEZs) along its southern coast to attract foreign capital and technology. Which of the following was the most prominent among them?
questions.explanation: Shenzhen, adjacent to Hong Kong, was designated China's first and most successful Special Economic Zone in 1980, serving as the experimental laboratory for market reforms.

questions.question: Which historic agreement signed in 1985 led to the gradual abolition of internal passport controls and common visa policies among most European countries?
questions.explanation: The Schengen Agreement was signed in June 1985 in Schengen, Luxembourg, leading to the creation of Europe's border-free Schengen Area.

questions.question: The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE), founded in 1976 under the leadership of Velupillai Prabhakaran, waged an armed campaign demanding:
options: A) Immediate merger of northern Sri Lanka into the Indian Union
B) The establishment of a Buddhist theocratic republic across Sri Lanka
C) An independent sovereign Tamil state (Tamil Eelam) in north-eastern Sri Lanka
D) Universal dual citizenship with Great Britain
questions.explanation: The LTTE fought an armed separatist war from 1983 to 2009 demanding the creation of an independent homeland for the Tamil minority called 'Tamil Eelam'.

questions.question: In October 2002, which Nepalese monarch dismissed the elected Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba and subsequently seized absolute executive power in February 2005?
questions.explanation: King Gyanendra dismissed the Prime Minister in 2002 and instituted direct royal rule in February 2005, triggering the massive 2006 democracy movement that ended the monarchy.

questions.question: The founder-president of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh who died under mysterious circumstances in detention in Srinagar in June 1953 while protesting the permit system for Jammu & Kashmir was:
questions.explanation: Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee entered Jammu & Kashmir without an entry permit in May 1953 to assert that the state was an integral part of India, dying in custody in Srinagar on 23 June 1953.

questions.question: In February 1948, the accession of the princely state of Junagadh to the Indian Union was formally ratified through:
options: A) A royal treaty signed by the Nawab before fleeing to Karachi
B) A popular plebiscite in which citizens overwhelmingly voted to join India
C) A military invasion ordered under the United Nations Security Council
D) An executive proclamation by the Governor General without public voting
questions.explanation: After the Nawab of Junagadh fled to Pakistan, the Government of India conducted a popular referendum (plebiscite) in February 1948 where 99.95% of voters chose accession to India.

questions.question:
Consider the following historical committees appointed to examine the demand for linguistic reorganisation of Indian states:
1. Linguistic Provinces Commission (Dhar Commission, 1948)
2. JVP Committee (Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya, 1948)
3. States Reorganisation Commission (Fazal Ali Commission, 1953)
Which of the following correctly describes the position taken by the Dhar Commission and the JVP Committee?
options: A) Both unconditionally recommended the immediate division of all provinces based purely on mother tongue.
B) The Dhar Commission supported linguistic division, while the JVP Committee rejected it.
C) Both rejected language as the immediate basis for the reorganisation of states, prioritizing national unity and economic development.
D) Both committees recommended transferring the decision entirely to the United Nations Trusteeship Council.
questions.explanation: The S.K. Dhar Commission (Dec 1948) advised against reorganisation on language grounds, emphasizing administrative convenience. The subsequent JVP Committee (April 1949) formally endorsed Dhar's view, advising postponement of linguistic states to preserve national unity.

questions.question: J.C. Kumarappa, an influential Gandhian economist, proposed an alternative development framework titled 'Economy of Permanence' which differed fundamentally from the Second Five Year Plan by advocating:
options: A) Total militarization of production under a central command economy.
B) Complete privatization of heavy industries with foreign multinational ownership.
C) Abolition of all agricultural subsidies to fund nuclear energy expansion.
D) Decentralized rural cottage production, environmental harmony, and village self-reliance rather than capital-intensive heavy industrialization.
questions.explanation: Kumarappa's 'Economy of Permanence' warned against the exploitation of nature and human beings through heavy, urbanized industrialization, advocating decentralized village industries and self-sufficient local economies.

questions.question: During the official visit of Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao to Beijing in September 1993, India and China signed which groundbreaking agreement to normalize relations along the disputed border?
options: A) Agreement on the Maintenance of Peace and Tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control (LAC)
B) Treaty of Perpetual Friendship and Boundary Demarcation
C) Joint Declaration on the Mutual Demilitarization of the McMahon Line
D) Sino-Indian Protocol on Non-Proliferation in South Asia
questions.explanation: On 7 September 1993, India and China signed the 'Agreement on the Maintenance of Peace and Tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control (LAC)' in Beijing, pledging to respect the LAC and reduce military forces along it.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In the 1971 Lok Sabha elections, opposition parties including the Samyukta Socialist Party, Praja Socialist Party, Bharatiya Jana Sangh, Swatantra Party, and Congress (O) formed an umbrella electoral pact known as the:
questions.explanation: The non-communist opposition parties formed the 'Grand Alliance' in the 1971 elections with the unified campaign plank of 'Indira Hatao', which Indira Gandhi famously countered with 'Garibi Hatao'.

questions.question: On 12 June 1975, which High Court judge delivered the historic ruling setting aside Indira Gandhi's election to the Lok Sabha from Rae Bareli on grounds of electoral malpractices, precipitating the declaration of Emergency?
questions.explanation: Justice Jagmohan Lal Sinha of the Allahabad High Court ruled on Raj Narain's election petition, declaring Indira Gandhi's 1971 election invalid due to misuse of government machinery.

questions.question: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution, adopted by the Shiromani Akali Dal at Anandpur Sahib in October 1973, primarily demanded:
options: A) The immediate armed secession of Punjab to create an independent state.
B) The abolition of the Constitution of India and implementation of a theocracy.
C) The merger of Jammu & Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh into Greater Punjab.
D) Restricting the Centre's role to defense, foreign relations, communications, and currency, with complete autonomy for the states.
questions.explanation: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution (1973) sought a redefinition of Centre-State relations, advocating genuine federalism where the Union government retained only defense, foreign affairs, currency, and communications.

questions.question: The grassroots campaign for the Right to Information in India was pioneered in Rajasthan in the 1990s by the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (MKSS) using which novel method of public accountability?
options: B) Armed gherao of legislative secretariats
C) Boycott of all union and state taxation
D) Indefinite strikes by government treasury clerks
questions.explanation: MKSS, founded by Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey, and Shankar Singh, organized 'Jan Sunwais' (public hearings) where village muster rolls and expenditure vouchers were read out aloud before local villagers to audit development funds.

questions.question:
Match the following historical events associated with the disintegration of the Soviet Union with their correct years:
(a) Mikhail Gorbachev becomes General Secretary of CPSU — 1. 1985
(b) Independence declaration by Lithuania — 2. 1990
(c) Hardline communist coup against Gorbachev — 3. August 1991
(d) Formal dissolution of the USSR by Russia, Belarus, and Ukraine — 4. December 1991
Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Gorbachev came to power in 1985. Lithuania declared independence in March 1990. The communist coup took place in August 1991. Yeltsin, Kravchuk, and Shushkevich signed the Belavezha Accords dissolving the USSR in December 1991.

questions.question: Under the Bali Concord II adopted in October 2003, the ASEAN leaders established the ASEAN Community resting upon three interrelated pillars. Which of the following is NOT one of these three pillars?
questions.explanation: The three pillars established at the 2003 Bali Summit are the ASEAN Political-Security Community (APSC), ASEAN Economic Community (AEC), and ASEAN Socio-Cultural Community (ASCC). There is no military alliance command.

questions.question: The second Secretary-General of the United Nations, who was posthumously awarded the Nobel Peace Prize after perishing in a plane crash in Northern Rhodesia in September 1961 during a peacekeeping mission, was:
questions.explanation: Dag Hammarskjöld of Sweden served as UN Secretary-General from 1953 until his death on 18 September 1961 while negotiating a ceasefire during the Congo Crisis. He received the Nobel Peace Prize posthumously.

questions.question:
The Strategic Arms Limitation Talks I (SALT I) concluded in Moscow in May 1972 between Richard Nixon and Leonid Brezhnev resulted in the signing of two landmark agreements:
1. The Anti-Ballistic Missile (ABM) Treaty
2. The Interim Agreement on the Limitation of Strategic Offensive Arms
Which of the following is an accurate statement about these agreements?
options: A) They mandated the complete elimination of all nuclear arsenals within five years.
B) They capped the number of strategic ballistic missile launchers and strictly limited the deployment of anti-ballistic missile defense systems.
C) They banned all research into conventional infantry weaponry across NATO and Warsaw Pact nations.
D) They authorized both superpowers to conduct unrestricted orbital nuclear detonations.
questions.explanation: SALT I froze the number of strategic ballistic missile launchers at existing levels and limited each superpower to two ABM deployment sites, preserving mutual assured destruction deterrence.

questions.question: Principle 21 of the 1972 Stockholm Declaration on the Human Environment established a fundamental tension in international environmental law by affirming that states have:
options: A) An absolute right to extract natural resources without any regard for cross-border pollution or ecological harm.
B) No sovereign right over their natural resources, placing all national forests under direct UN administration.
C) The legal obligation to shut down all industrial manufacturing within twenty years.

D) The sovereign right to exploit their own resources pursuant to their environmental policies, coupled with the responsibility to ensure that activities within their jurisdiction do not cause damage to the environment of other states.
questions.explanation: Principle 21 of the 1972 Stockholm Declaration balances state sovereignty over resource exploitation with the customary legal duty not to cause transboundary environmental harm.
